title: One Password, Every Door

audience.who: corporate employees in any role who log in to work systems every day
audience.knows: they have passwords and that phishing exists; most reuse a password somewhere and assume one leak only costs one account
audience.cares_about: not being the person a breach started with, and keeping their own accounts safe without extra hassle

outcome: After watching, the viewer can check whether any work password is reused elsewhere, replace it with a unique one kept in a password manager, turn on multi-factor authentication, and report a suspicious login prompt or leak notice straight away.
through_line: A breach rarely needs a genius: one reused password, leaked somewhere unrelated, opens every door that shares it, and two plain habits (a unique password per account, a second factor) close those doors before anyone tries them.

arc_plan.what: Night, one employee's ordinary login; we learn the password was already out there, leaked from an unrelated personal site.
arc_plan.source_anchor: knowledge sheet: how credentials leak from third-party breaches

arc_plan.what: Follow that one password through the night to see how it became a company-wide breach, and what would have stopped it at each step.
Why reuse matters: a leaked username and password pair is tried automatically against many other services.
Section 1, leaked and tried: the pair lands in a dump and is tested at scale against work logins; it works because it was reused.
Section 2, spread: once inside with a valid account, the attacker moves to other systems and accounts, so one login becomes many.
arc_plan.source_anchor: knowledge sheet: lateral movement after account compromise

arc_plan.what: Section 3, the doors that would have held: a unique password per account, a password manager to make that practical, multi-factor authentication blocking a correct password used by someone else.
arc_plan.source_anchor: knowledge sheet: password manager and MFA guidance

arc_plan.what: A short scenario the viewer judges: which habit stops the attack at which step.
arc_plan.source_anchor: knowledge sheet: password manager and MFA guidance

arc_plan.what: What to do this week, including reporting an unexpected login prompt or breach notice to the security team.
Return to the opening login at night, replayed with the habits in place: the leaked password opens nothing.

must_cover.what: Passwords leak from third-party breaches outside the company's control, and leaked credentials are collected and shared.
Reused passwords enable credential stuffing: automated trying of leaked username and password pairs on other services.
From one compromised account an attacker can spread to other systems and accounts.
A unique password for every account, made practical by a password manager.
Multi-factor authentication stops a correct but stolen password from being enough.
Report unexpected login prompts, MFA requests you did not start, or breach notices to the security team promptly.

must_avoid: sensational or fear-mongering framing, hacker cliches, hooded figures, scrolling green code
breach statistics or costs without a sourced fact
naming or implying a real company or real incident as this case
blaming the employee; the case is about habits, not shame
learning-styles claims, made-up testimony presented as real
an agenda opening, or an opening that starts by explaining terms
example_posture: One fictional employee and one fictional company carried the whole way; every step of the attack is something that happens to this one password, plainly hypothetical, never presented as a real incident.
visual_direction: Cinematic night case file: a single key light, silhouettes, slow camera pushes; the password as a physical object we can follow from door to door; doors or locks that open as the password spreads and stay shut when the habits are in place; a before and after of the same night.
voice_note: A calm investigator walking a colleague through the case: measured, serious, never dramatic for its own sake; short sentences, plain words, no jargon left unexplained.
open_questions: Topic mode with no source document: every arc anchor points at the knowledge sheet the fact-finder will build; any claim it cannot ground is dropped.
Promise and payoff are framed from the requester's notes rather than a source.

from_user: story: reused password leaked, tried, spread, and the habits that stop it
